{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement form

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The agreement is well drafted in several places that matter to us — the liability cap, assignment and change of control, renewal mechanics, the performance warranty, audit rights and Vendor insurance all sit at our preferred position and need no redlines.

The problems are concentrated in two areas. First, **the agreement has no indemnification clause at all**: Section 20 is absent from the document even though Sections 9.3 and 19.4 depend on it, and Section 9.3 cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5," leaving a broken reference. That is walk-away territory and must be fixed by inserting Section 20.

Second, the agreement loads a cluster of one-sided restrictions onto us that our playbook treats as walk-away items and that **contradict Section 12.3**, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment. These are the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay in Section 2.1, the disclose-and-match obligation in Section 7.2 (which is both a de facto exclusivity/ROFR and an MFN running against us), the 24-month unlimited-scope Customer non-compete and the 24-month full no-hire in the two Sections 12.4. Deleting or narrowing them restores internal consistency as well as our playbook position.

Three further gaps round out the list: Vendor owns every Deliverable we pay for under Section 14.2 with only a revocable, term-limited licence back; there is no Customer termination for convenience across a three-year committed term; there is no post-termination transition assistance or data return/deletion obligation; and Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, in direct conflict with Section 28.2's submission to the New York County courts.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 20 absent (cross-referenced at §§ 9.3, 19.4; see § 19.5) | No indemnity anywhere; broken cross-reference to § 20.5. Insert Section 20. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable; only a revocable, term-limited licence to us. Flip ownership with assignment; § 14.3 Vendor Technology unaffected. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with full Excluded Claims set (§ 21.3). No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Customer may assign to Affiliate/successor on notice; Vendor restricted; no repricing on our change of control (§ 24.4). No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Disclose-and-match before engaging another provider is a de facto exclusivity/ROFR, unlimited in scope and term. Delete. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 | No Customer-payable liquidated damages or exit fee; § 27.3 permits termination without penalty with refund. No redline. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 14.2 | Deliverable licence is revocable, non-transferable, term-limited and omits Affiliates/contractors, unlike §§ 13.1–13.3. Conform to Section 13. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (non-compete) | 24-month post-term, undefined scope, unlimited territory, acquisitions barred. Delete and rely on § 12.3. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 9.3 (see § 2.1, § 8.1) | No Customer convenience right across a three-year take-or-pay term. Add 30-day right with pro-rata refund as new § 9.4; conform § 2.1. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 | One audit per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, no system access; cost-shifting only above 5% underpayment. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts; conflicts with § 28.2 (New York County). Substitute New York law and forum. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor; conflicts with § 12.3. Delete. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay expressly without reduction or termination rights. Replace with pay-for-what-is-ordered. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (no-hire) | One-sided 24-month full no-hire covering all Vendor employees, overriding general-advertising carve-outs. Narrow to mutual 12-month non-solicit. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 | Successive 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3% (§ 8.3). No redline. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 (see § 16.5) | No transition assistance, export window or certified deletion; § 16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11. Insert new § 10.3. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 | Professional/workmanlike and conformity warranties, hosted Services warranted for the full subscription term, non-exclusive remedies; disclaimer limited to implied warranties. No redline. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL, workers' compensation, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber/privacy USD 5M through term plus one year. No redline. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following are walk-away positions under our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (missing Section 20).** With no IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct indemnity, we carry infringement and regulatory exposure ourselves. We propose the preferred package: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; customary exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications); standard notice/control/cooperation procedure; a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law; and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in § 20.5 to repair the § 9.3 cross-reference.
2. **Section 2.1 take-or-pay.** A three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year commitment "without reduction or termination rights" is squarely walk-away. Fallback if a commitment is commercially required: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
3. **Section 7.2 disclose-and-match.** Walk-away as both exclusivity/ROFR and Customer-side MFN; unlimited as to product, term and comparability. Deletion is the smallest fix and restores consistency with § 12.3.
4. **Section 12.4 Customer non-compete.** 24 months post-term, undefined competing scope, unlimited territory, acquisitions expressly barred. Delete; we can discuss a narrowed restriction tied to a specific named product if Vendor identifies one.
5. **Section 12.4 no-hire.** A one-sided 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees regardless of how they apply. We have narrowed it to the fallback (mutual, 12 months from the end of the individual's involvement, personnel directly involved in the Services, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no-hire deleted); our preferred position remains no restriction on us.
6. **Section 28.1 Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts.** Outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and an exclusive foreign forum. We align 28.1 with 28.2 (New York law, New York County courts), leaving §§ 28.2–28.3 intact.
7. **Section 14.2 Deliverable licence.** A revocable, term-limited grant to work product we commissioned and paid for approaches walk-away under the licence-scope rule; it is addressed together with the ownership flip.

---

## Next steps

1. **Confirm commercial mandate on Section 2.1.** Whether we can accept any minimum commitment, and if so whether the 12-month reducible fallback with a true-up is acceptable, drives the § 2.1 and § 9.4 redlines together.
2. **Send the redline as a package.** Insert Section 20 (indemnification, including § 20.5 remedies); insert new § 10.3 (transition assistance and Customer Data return/deletion, with a 90-day fallback offered in comment); insert new § 9.4 (30-day convenience termination with pro-rata refund) and conform § 2.1; flip § 14.2 Deliverable ownership with assignment and conform the Deliverable licence to Section 13; delete § 7.2 and the § 12.4 non-compete; narrow the § 12.4 no-hire; and substitute New York law and forum in § 28.1.
3. **Flag the drafting defects separately to Vendor's counsel.** The absent Section 20, the absent Section 11 referenced by § 16.5, the empty Section 23, the duplicated Section 12.4 numbering and the 28.1/28.2 forum conflict are internal inconsistencies rather than positions, and framing them that way should speed acceptance.
4. **Use Section 12.3 as the lever.** Vendor has already acknowledged there that we have made no exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment; every deletion we seek in items 2–5 above simply gives that acknowledgement effect.
5. **Do not reopen the compliant clauses.** Sections 8, 18, 19, 21, 22 and 24 sit at or above our preferred position; we should protect them in any exchange of drafts.

*Note: verification of the underlying findings was not completed; section references and conclusions above are drawn solely from the findings supplied.*"}
